results.name: Assisted_Facilities_in_Ohio_NEW
results.title: Assisted Living / Residential Care Facilities in Ohio
results.description:
In Ohio, assisted living facilities are officially known as Residential Care Facilities and are licensed by the Ohio Department of Health. These facilities offer a combination of housing and personal care services, providing an alternative to nursing homes for individuals who need assistance with daily living activities but don't require 24-hour skilled nursing care.

results.title: Nursing Homes Licensed and Certified in Ohio
results.description:
Certified and licensed nursing homes are facilities that meet state and federal regulations for providing skilled nursing, rehabilitation, or long-term care. In Ohio, the Ohio Department of Health is responsible for licensing and certifying nursing homes to ensure they provide a safe and high-quality environment for residents.

results.name: Federally_Qualified_Health_Care_Centers_in_Ohio_NEW
results.title: Federally Qualified Healthcare Centers (FQHC) in Ohio
results.description:
FQHC stands for Federally Qualified Health Center, which is a type of primary care clinic that receives federal funds to provide healthcare to underserved communities. To be designated an FQHC, a health center must serve a high-need area and be governed by a community board where at least 51% of the members are patients of the health center. FQHCs offer comprehensive primary care services and must not turn any patient away due to their inability to pay.

results.name: Dialysis_End_Stage_Renal_Facilities_in_Ohio_NEW
results.title: Dialysis / End Stage Renal Facilities in Ohio
results.description:
Dialysis ESRD facilities are clinics that provide dialysis care to individuals with kidney failure, and they can be hospital-based or freestanding. These facilities must meet health and safety standards set by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and are subject to government certification and inspection. They offer different dialysis modalities, such as in-center and home dialysis, to accommodate patient needs.

results.title: ODH Health Facility Information
results.description:
An export of the Ohio Public Health Data Warehouse, known as Ohio OneSource.
http://publicapps.odh.ohio.gov/EDW/DataCatalog
The Ohio Public Health Data Warehouse is a self-service online tool where anyone can obtain the most recent public health data available about Ohio.

Citation:
Please use the following citation in any publication or release which uses or references data from the Warehouse: "These data were provided by the Ohio Department of Health. The Department specifically disclaims responsibility for any analyses, interpretations or conclusions".
Information for authorized public health personnel and IRB-approved researchers to access ODH’s secure data warehouse can be found here.  

http://publicapps.odh.ohio.gov/EDW/DataBrowser/Browse/OhioOneSource

Ohio OneSource
Category:Data Quality 
Latest Update:5/21/2018 
Description: Find licensed providers. 
Contact Email: informatics@odh.ohio.gov

Purpose:

This tool is intended to provide a “one stop shop” to search, filter, and extract information for all licensed healthcare facilities within the State of Ohio. Examples of provider types include, but are not limited to the following:
  • AS - Ambulatory Surgical Center
  • CI - Correctional Institution
  • CL - Clinic
  • CT- Chemical Treatment
  • DU - Dialysis Unit
  • EM - Emergency Medical Service
  • FA - First Aid Department
  • HH - Home Health Care
  • HS - Hospital
  • IM - Imaging / Diagnostic
  • LA - Laboratory
  • MG - Medical Gas Services
  • MH - Mental Health
  • NH - Nursing Home
  • PC - Practitioner Corporation
  • PMC - Pain Management Clinic
  • PS - Pharmacy Services
  • PT - Physical Therapy
  • TE - Teaching
  • UR - Urgent Care
*Data for this facility lookup tool is provided by the Ohio Board of Pharmacy and the Ohio Department of Health.
